newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonos closed on Monday at a new high, although a little below the day's record peak of 112.60, following other markets in subdued holiday trade.
While a dealer reported last-minute buying by a few domestic investment trusts, they said the year was virtually concluded.
"The market looks ahead to close the year around these levels," a Madrid dealer said.
"We need to see how foreign markets start 1997," one said.
On Tuesday, Spain's Meff will celebrate New Year's Eve with an early close at 1200 GMT. The local currency market will be closed, a Bank of Spain official said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was trading at the close at around 107 basis points, down from 111 late on Friday, just above its all-time record low of 104 bps set on December 16.
"At 100 basis points there will be strong resistance, and I certainly do not expect this spread to break below 90 bps," an economist in Madrid said.
The short end appears less risky.

"Buying and staying in the three-year segment is less dangerous and more rewarding. It's a matter of when and how the Bank of Spain will cut. Nobody doubts short-term interest rates will fall," a dealer added.
